premises.text: Analysts spend a large share of time hunting market research across fragmented Google and aggregator portals that miss or bury the right reports
premises.evidence_span: The average analyst spends 19 percent of their day researching. For every five that show up to work, one shows up to search

premises.text: UX unified industry classification is ~10x more granular than NAICS for mapping industries and adjacencies
premises.evidence_span: UX is T4's Unified Industry Classification System, a method of classifying industries that is 10 times more granular than NAICS, the industry standard

premises.text: Tom human-in-the-loop indexing aggregates a complete market-research set per industry and indexes quantitative data inside reports
premises.evidence_span: Tom is T4's proprietary, human-in-the-loop indexing process. Tom ensures that we aggregate a complete set of market research within each industry and index the quantitative data within each report

premises.text: SaaS search tells analysts which paid or free reports contain needed data (with sources/page numbers), sold per-seat to consulting/investing/strategy analysts
premises.evidence_span: A web platform lets analysts quickly find comprehensive industry data. Tell T4 what you're looking for, T4 tells you what reports contain the data you need

value.text: Find the exact industry data needed in seconds instead of hours of portal searching
value.evidence_span: What normally takes hours, Sarah just did in 30 seconds

causal_links.evidence_span: companies are paying analysts billions of dollars every year to look for market research
This is possible because UX and Tom enabled T4 to comprehensively index granular data that AI does not have the capability to process
you want to save hours of research every single day

notes: UX and Tom kept as separately named competencies that could fail independently (enumeration rule 2 / tie-break), grouped in one indexing domain because they must be learned together for the search product. Pricing amount folded into SaaS premise.
